Subject: Velocity MAP: Benchmark & quant/kernel results + close timeline

Simon —

Following up on our discovery, attached is the proposed benchmarking plan we discussed for the Velocity MAP. High level goals:
- Deliver a MAP-aligned performance report (latency, throughput, TTFT, concurrency) and quant/kernel profiles for the two model families you asked about (open-llm-x1 and open-llm-x1-compact).
- Surface regressions vs the FP16 baseline when running INT8/INT4 quantized variants plus kernel-level differences that impact TTFT and long-context throughput.
- Provide actionable rollout guidance (canary config, batching, kernel pins) so you can evaluate in your staging environment prior to commit.

Acceptance criteria (please confirm):
1) TTFT (time-to-first-token) ≤ 200ms at single-request concurrency for 1k token context on target hardware.
2) Sustained throughput for 4 concurrent streams: at least 60 tokens/sec per stream.
3) No more than 5% quality delta (per your eval set) against the FP16 baseline for INT8; flag INT4 as exploratory.

Planned milestones (MAP timeline):
- 11/16: Baseline FP16/BF16 runs + kernel profile capture (initial).
- 11/20: INT8/INT4 quant runs + regression checks.
- 11/24: Internal review and write-up.
- 11/30: Deliver MAP artifact (benchmarks + recommended canary).

Attachments: velocity_map_benchmark_plan.md (scope + test harness), kernel_profile_summary.pdf (kernel capture checklist), raw_latency_throughput.csv (template).

Can you confirm the acceptance numbers above and the target close date you have in mind? You mentioned wanting to close before year-end — are you aiming for 12/05 sign-off?

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before you run the INT8/INT4 pass:
- Baseline hardware: we will test on AWS g5.12xlarge (A10G equivalent) and a private DGX-like host (A100 40GB). Please include both.
- Workloads: two profiles: (A) chat style — 120-token prompts → 600-token generations (TTFT critical), (B) long-form synth — 1k prompts → 2k generations (throughput critical).
- For regression checks: please run your automatic eval harness against our sample eval set (attached separately to HubSpot deal). INT8 regressions must be flagged by token position (early vs late) and by answer-level metrics.

Timeline: we are pushing internally to have a procurement decision by 12/03 so we can start integration in mid-December. If you can deliver final numbers by 11/30, that should let us complete procurement by 12/03. Are those dates workable?

Also, please include kernel-level traces (per-step op times) — we need to understand if any INT8 kernels are causing TTFT spikes.

-Simon

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 10:15 AM Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Simon —
> 
> Following up on our discovery, attached is the proposed benchmarking plan we discussed for the Velocity MAP. High level goals:
> - Deliver a MAP-aligned performance report (latency, throughput, TTFT, concurrency) and quant/kernel profiles for the two model families you asked about (open-llm-x1 and open-llm-x1-compact).

Hi Simon — thanks for the details. We completed the runs across both hardware targets and the two workload profiles. Summary of the key findings (full artifacts attached):

1) TTFT (time-to-first-token) — chat profile (120→600 tokens):
- FP16 (A100-40GB): median TTFT = 110ms; 95th = 185ms.
- BF16 (A100-40GB): median TTFT = 115ms; 95th = 190ms (negligible difference).
- INT8 (A100-40GB, per-channel quant): median TTFT = 140ms; 95th = 280ms (95th driven by kernel fallback for long context).
- INT4 (A100-40GB): median TTFT = 220ms; 95th = 520ms — exploratory, quality loss >10% on eval set.

2) Throughput / concurrency (long-form profile 1k→2k tokens):
- FP16 (g5.12xlarge): sustained throughput = 420 tokens/sec at concurrency=4.
- INT8 (g5.12xlarge): sustained throughput = 520 tokens/sec at concurrency=4 (good win for throughput), but observed TTFT spikes under cold-start and with kernel switching.

3) Kernel profile notes (per-step op times attached in kernel_profile_summary.pdf):
- A specific GEMM kernel in the INT8 path for sequences >1k caused spikes in first-step latency due to an on-demand kernel selection path. Pinning a precompiled INT8 kernel reduced 95th TTFT by ~140ms at the cost of +3% avg token latency.
- BF16 path uses the same fusion kernels as FP16 — behavior closely matches FP16 for TTFT and throughput.

4) Regression checks (eval harness vs your provided set):
- INT8 per-answer quality delta: median 2.8% relative drop vs FP16; within your 5% acceptance.
- INT4: median 12.4% drop — we recommend not using INT4 in production for your use case.
- We flagged 7 prompt IDs with >8% drop in INT8 tied to late-token hallucinations — included in raw_latency_throughput.csv and a small prompt-level diff report.

Recommendations / MAP deliverables:
- Canary config: INT8 quant + kernel pin for sequences >512, small prefix cache enabled, batching capped at 8 tokens to keep TTFT tight.
- Fallback policy: if 95th TTFT > 350ms, route to BF16 FP16 pool.
- Next validation: run a 48-hour stochastic run on your staging pool with your live-ish traffic (we can schedule 12/01-12/02) and deliver a canary report by 12/03.

Attachments: kernel_profile_summary.pdf (kernel traces + pin notes), raw_latency_throughput.csv (per-run numbers), velocity_map_benchmark_plan.md (updated with run parameters).

Let us know if you'd like us to run the pinned INT8 config on your DGX host; we'll need SSH access or upload of a small container (we can provide an ephemeral signed S3 link).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
